target_customer: African fintechs, banks and digital businesses needing KYC, KYB and fraud checks
problem: Innovators struggle to source APIs and government data to verify customer identity and prevent fraud in African markets.
business_model: Usage-based identity verification and fraud API plus no-code dashboard
product_category: Identity verification, KYC and anti-fraud infrastructure

founders.background_notes: Per YC page; education not listed.

technical_complexity.rationale: Aggregating government data lookups, biometrics and risk scoring across countries is integration heavy but uses established components.

defensibility.rationale: Government data integrations and compliance certifications (NDPR, ISO, SOC per its site) take time to replicate; rivals offer identical services.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No acquisition found; the market stayed fragmented with several African KYC rivals raising seeds.

market_need_then: Fast growth of African fintech and tightening KYC rules created demand for verification APIs; competitor rounds in 2022 reflect investor interest.

identity.visual_style: enterprise product site with customer logos

brand_strength.rationale: Trade coverage (TechMoran, TechCrunch mentions) but no sourced evidence of brand pull; name meaning unknown.

outcome_analysis: Dojah remained active with about 30 staff on the YC page and a broad KYC and anti-fraud product suite. No shutdown, acquisition or layoff news was found. Aggregators show only about $510K raised, so growth appears modest and capital efficient, but no primary source confirms funding or revenue.
notes: Funding unverified: CB Insights lists $510K over 5 rounds (accelerator rounds, latest Nov 2023) and investors including Visa Africa Accelerator, Plug and Play and YC; Startuplist shows $0 total. Single aggregator, so no rounds recorded. Founded 2020 or 2021 depending on source.
